title: Drag Race Physics Simulator
description: Two cars line up on a straight drag strip. The user configures mass, engine force, drag coefficient, and tire friction for each vehicle independently, then launches them in a physics-simulated quarter-mile race. Real-time telemetry overlays show velocity, acceleration, and distance for both cars as they race side by side.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements a drag race physics simulator. Load CarConcept.glb in the left lane and ferrari.glb in the right lane on a flat textured road plane (at least 400 units long with lane markings). Use GLTFLoader from a CDN. Position the camera at a slightly elevated rear-quarter angle behind both cars so both are visible; the camera should smoothly follow the leading car during the race. Add directional light, ambient light, and subtle fog for depth. Create an HTML overlay control panel with sliders for each car: mass (800-2000 kg), engine force (3000-15000 N), aerodynamic drag coefficient (0.25-0.55), and rolling friction coefficient (0.01-0.04). Each slider must display its current numeric value and validate min/max bounds. Add a Start Race button that is disabled until all 8 parameters have been explicitly adjusted by the user at least once. On start, simulate Newtonian physics each frame: net force equals engine force minus aerodynamic drag (0.5 * Cd * A * rho * v^2, use A=2.2 and rho=1.225) minus rolling friction (mu * m * g). Integrate acceleration to velocity and velocity to position using delta time. Animate each GLB model translating forward along the road according to its computed position. Spin each car's wheels proportionally to velocity if wheel meshes are found. Display a real-time HUD for each car showing current speed in km/h, acceleration in m/s^2, and distance traveled in meters. The race ends when either car crosses 402 meters (quarter mile). On finish, freeze the simulation, display the winner with elapsed time for both cars, and show a Restart button that resets positions and re-enables parameter editing. Ensure all parameter changes are blocked during an active race. The road should have a visible start line and finish line. Add a countdown sequence of 3-2-1-GO with visible text before cars begin moving.
